cumleler: Is the air-bone gap on an audiogram always real?
A bone vibrator stimulates both cochleae almost equally.
An unmasked threshold may come from the better cochlea.
A sensorineural loss can then look like a conductive one.
Mask the other ear, and bone thresholds may rise; the gap closes.
So the test ear needs masking when the gap exceeds ten decibels.
